title: JFrog reference token as a bare 64-character cmVmd value, an 8-character-prefix value, or a bare 128-character value
summary: A bare cmVmd value with 59 characters after the prefix, a bare cmVmdGtu value with 56 after the prefix, and a bare 128-character alphanumeric value.
rationale: JFrog's Identity Tokens page states the pattern cmVmd plus 59 alphanumeric characters and calls reference tokens short (64 characters); its Access Tokens page describes the admin-scoped reference token as a 128-character key (claims identity-page-pattern-64, access-page-128-character-key, length-64-versus-128-conflict: unresolved, the pages do not say whether they describe different forms, eras or one stale figure). The 8-character prefix cmVmdGtu is one artifact's lead (eight-character-prefix-single-artifact), and the introduction version differs between 7.38.4 and 7.38.10 (introduction-version-conflict). The handoff for this row says not to author a shape-only expectation. No outcome is asserted.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Whether a bare cmVmd value of 64 characters, a cmVmdGtu value, or a bare 128-character value is a JFrog reference token is not settled by JFrog's own pages, which conflict. Settled by a JFrog length history per release with dates, or a dated archive snapshot of the Access Tokens page.

sources.supports: Unlike a regular JWT token, reference tokens follow this pattern: .*\bcmVmd[A-Za-z0-9]{59}\b.* , starting with cmVmd followed by 59 more alphanumeric characters.
Reference tokens are short (64 characters) - unlike JWT Tokens, reference tokens can be used with clients that do not support long tokens or passwords.
